newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk group boosted nickel exports in 96.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk group boosted nickel exports in 96.

text.p: Russia's RAO Norilsky Nikel metals group exported 104,861 tonnes of nickel in 1996, which was 62 percent of total sales of 168,861 tonnes and 20 percent higher than exports in 1995, a company statement said on Tuesday.
The Norilsk group also exported 241,407 tonnes of copper last year, which was over 70 percent of its total sales of 342,934 tonnes and over double the volume exported in 1995, it added.
"Due to the continuing fall in solvent demand for the group's products within the country, it was forced to increase the volumes of metal exports in 1996," the statement said.

A company spokesman said he could not give forecasts for how much metal the group would export in 1997, but said base metals demand in Russia was unlikely to rise significantly this year. Norilsk has outlined plans to boost nickel production by 20 percent in 1997 to 213,000 tonnes and copper output by nine percent to 370,000 tonnes.
"In general our management would like to sell more on the domestic market, but only in 1998 and 1999 is there likely to be any significant pick-up in metals demand in Russia," the spokesman said.

He could not specify whether last year's nickel and copper exports included shipments to Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), but added that the big majority would have gone to non-CIS countries.
